messages:
mike: heads-up: on canary today we saw a 12-18% throughput drop when FP8 was enabled on a subset of H100 nodes. looks like a kernel selection flip under microbatch load.
sofia: Ugh. repro steps?
mike: ran loadtest with microbatch=4, seq=2048, kv-cache enabled. when the runtime picks the FP8-optimized GEMM kernel we get lower occupancy, int8 path was better in this case.
cj: do you have traces? can you paste the kernel timeline?
mike: yeah, attaching quick snippet from profiler: 
```
kernel_choice: fp8_gemm_8x128   63%
kernel_choice: int8_gemm_16x64  35%
latency_p50: 42ms -> 49ms after flip
throughput: 820 req/s -> 670 req/s
kv_evictions/sec: 0.9 -> 3.7
```
erin: kv_evictions jump is interesting — could be KV warmup getting invalidated by slower kernels, increasing cache churn.
sofia: can you confirm transformer-engine flags that were used? I remember some TE heuristics prefer FP8 kernels only if sequence-length distribution is narrow.
mike: TE flags: `--te-fp8=auto --te-precompile=on --te-sparsity=off`
perf-bot: profile summary uploaded: https://internal/prof/3567004444 (contains hw counters + nvprof timeline) :robot_face:
cj: quick hypothesis: FP8 kernel has lower per-thread utilization for this batchshape; throughput wins for int8 since microbatching interleaves better. Also FP8 path adds small quant/dequant overhead that matters at these microbatch sizes.
ero: (typo: erin meant) we should try microbatch=2 and microbatch=8 to see sensitivity. also run with KV-cache disabled to isolate.
mike: ran both: microbatch=2 -> performance back to baseline even with FP8 kernels; microbatch=8 -> worse than mb4. With kv disabled, throughput drop reduces to ~5%.
sofia: sounds like a tipping point at mb shape ~3-5 where kernel selection matters + KV behavior amplifies.
cj: temporary mitigation options: 1) force kernel safelist to prefer int8 for these shapes 2) adjust TE heuristics to require higher occupancy for FP8 3) pin microbatch to 2 for canary traffic 4) tune KV warmup to be more tolerant of small tail latency increases.
mike: I tried forcing `kernel_policy=prefer_int8_for_mb<=4` and saw throughput back to +3% over baseline. patch diff here: 
```json
{"kernel_policy":"prefer_int8_for_mb<=4"}
```
sofia: good quick fix. longer term we need an automated decision function that considers kv_eviction rate + occupancy + microbatch. maybe a tiny cost model.
erin: agree. Also we should add a perf regression alert that triggers when kv_evictions/sec spikes > 2x baseline on kernel flip.
perf-bot: alert rule suggestion posted to #eng-sre.
cj: action items: mike to open a PR for kernel-policy fallback (WIP), sofia to add occupancy threshold to TE heuristics, erin to add alert and run a 24h canary with mb2 and mb4. i'll own postmortem if this becomes a regression.
mike: opening PR now: https://git/repo/pull/4123 - includes telemetry hooks for kv_eviction and per-kernel occupancy stats.
sofia: let's also capture a couple of long traces with nvtx around the quant/dequant to see CPU overhead.
erin: assigned canary run to @aqa-team for 24h.
mike: thanks. will follow up with the nvprof outputs and a short writeup. :thumbsup:
